dimension_1.justification: The design exhibits a clean, unidirectional layered architecture (API Router -> Domain Service -> Data Repository -> Persistence Models/Base) that strictly conforms to existing xhs-campaign-service conventions. Boundaries are well-defined: business rules and FSM validations live exclusively in the service layer, repositories are query-only and asynchronous, and Celery handles asynchronous background processing. There are no circular dependencies, and horizontal scalability is preserved through stateless API design and database-backed optimistic concurrency.

dimension_2.justification: RESTful conventions and HTTP semantics are executed flawlessly. All 11 endpoints provide explicit request/response schemas with field constraints, types, and cross-field validations. The API specifies URI versioning (/api/v1/), standardized ErrorResponse mappings for domain exceptions (403, 404, 409, 422), robust pagination (PaginatedResponse[T]), and explicit authentication/role/ownership requirements per route.

dimension_3.justification: The data model is production-ready and fully detailed. It incorporates all required domain entities (campaigns and campaign_status_logs), inherits standard base mixins (Base, TimestampMixin, SoftDeleteMixin), and uses proper types and constraints (UUID string PKs via generate_uuid(), Numeric(12,2) for CNY currency, DateTime(timezone=True), and JSONB). Query performance is prioritized with targeted B-tree indexes, including a compound index (owner_id, status, created_at DESC) to meet the sub-200ms p95 SLA and a partial index for active marketplace campaigns.

dimension_4.justification: The design adheres to all aspects of the existing microservice context. It faithfully integrates FastAPI dependencies (CurrentUser, require_role, _get_service factory), async SQLAlchemy 2.0 with asyncpg, existing exception classes, and Celery background workers. All integration points (internal UserRepository, external NotificationService, Redis cache, and future Application module) include explicit interface signatures, protocol definitions, and resilient failure handling.

dimension_5.justification: Trade-off analysis is exemplary. Seven major architectural decisions (such as optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking, dual-table audit trail vs event sourcing, and two-tier deadline enforcement) are thoroughly evaluated with concrete alternatives, rejection rationales, and performance implications. Four critical operational risks (concurrency races, timezone drift, message broker outages, and pagination scale) are matched with specific, practical mitigations.

scores.overall_assessment: This is an exceptional, production-grade technical design that comprehensively fulfills all functional requirements and user stories while seamlessly adopting existing system conventions. It addresses critical operational realities—such as concurrent edits, audit logging, and deadline enforcement—with sound architectural patterns and zero notable omissions.
